prompts:
Create byar-b.png, a production animation sprite sheet for Riley Wheel Brawl 2.0. Use attached Image 1 master-side.png as the LOCKED character design reference, matching exactly his face, short dark hair grey temples, gaunt stern 40-year-old face, steel armor and mail, white muddy ragged cloak and tabard, golden left-breast sunburst and two rank knots, brown boots, long straight steel longsword with gilded crossguard, and white kite shield with golden sunburst and gilded rim. Match reference ink and shading precisely.
Canvas MUST be 1536x1024 landscape, genuinely transparent RGBA background, no painted backdrop, no ground shadow. Exactly EIGHT separate full-body drawings arranged TWO rows of FOUR, reading order. Four equal 384x512 cells per row, clear transparent gaps, no overlapping cells. Same body scale in all poses, maximize size within cells while keeping whole swords, shields, cloak, boots and head within margins. Shared boot baseline near y=490 top row and y=1000 bottom row. All face LEFT, profile/slight 3/4. Every frame a distinct original drawing, no duplicates or mirroring. Keep sword blade length and shield size/shape identical relative to body in every frame, including foreshortening where needed.
Style: hand-drawn HD 2D fighting-game art in spirit of Streets of Rage 4; strong near-black/dark brown outer ink, finer inner ink, clean cel shading 2-3 steps with subtle painterly gradients. Rich grounded colors. Soft upper-left key, subtle cool right rim, moderate shading. Not pixel, 3D, photoreal, or chibi. Kid friendly no blood.
Top row from left:
1 COMBO BACKHAND: rising backhand slash toward LEFT, right sword arm sweeping long sword diagonally from low to high, blade now ascending up-left; shield left arm guards torso, twisting shoulders.
2 COMBO THRUST: deep forward lunge LEFT, front leftward boot bent knee, rear leg extended, right sword arm fully extended LEFT, long blade horizontal point straight left, shield tucked.
3 PARRY STANCE bait: standing tall, shield raised square ahead LEFT, right sword held low behind his right hip, smug narrow-eyed confidence.
4 PARRY: left-arm shield angled snapped outward LEFT to deflect, right sword pulled back preparing counter, distinct weight shift.
Bottom row from left:
5 RIPOSTE: fast LOW lunging counter-thrust LEFT, deeply crouched torso, right arm extended low with sword pointing left, shield raised protectively.
6 RIPOSTE RECOVERY: stepping backward into guard, torso rising, sword pulled back angled up-left, shield guarding forward, distinct from frame 3.
7 TAUNT: upright sneering, LEFT shield hand visibly beckons enemy with fingers while shield remains attached by forearm straps, RIGHT sword points down with tip off baseline.
8 ACCUSE: mouth open shouting, right arm and sword points straight LEFT at enemy, shield lowered alongside left leg; upright tall confrontational pose distinct from thrust lunge.
Anatomy in every drawing: exactly two arms, two legs, two booted feet, anatomically correct five-finger hands (occlusion allowed). No effects, dust, motion lines, text, labels, numbers, borders or grid. Preserve true transparent alpha, including between figures.

Edit the attached eight-character sprite sheet. Preserve all eight character drawings and their two rows of four layout and 1536x1024 size. The ONLY essential edit is REMOVE THE ENTIRE BROWN/BLACK/GRAY GRADIENT BACKGROUND. This is a background-extraction task: every pixel outside the actual character, armor, cloak, shield and sword silhouettes must be genuinely transparent with alpha 0. Do not retain or recreate any backdrop. No shadows, no floor. Keep character pixels opaque alpha 255 with antialiased edges. Output a transparent PNG sprite sheet. Also keep LEFT facing eight distinct poses matching master character design. Do not paint a checkerboard. The empty regions and all gaps between limbs and figures must be alpha zero.
inspection_note: Eight figures, four per row, all face left. 1536x1024 RGBA with true zero-alpha background. Weapon length and equipment handedness vary across poses; exact locked-design consistency is imperfect.
